notes: Page 2 shows steps 1-3. Step 1: black 2x4 plate (b1). Step 2: two dark grey side-handle plates (b2, b3) are attached under the plate, and two trans-orange round plates (b4, b5) go on the back right studs. Step 3: yellow bracket (b6) at the right end of the plate.
The pictures are small, so the exact placement of b2, b3 and b6 is my best guess.
Step 3 is drawn without the orange plates. I assumed they stay on the model and that the bracket rests only on b1. This may need correcting on the next page.

Page 3 shows steps 4-7. Step 4: yellow 2x3 plate (b7) on the base plate b1. Step 5: two dark grey round bricks (b8, b9) at the left end of b1. Step 6: yellow mudguard (b10) at the left, then a yellow clip plate (b11) with a trans-yellow tile (b12) on top. Step 7: black grate slope (b13) on the yellow plate, then a trans-red round plate (b14) on it.
The pictures are small, so the exact positions and the choice of parts for steps 4-5 are best guesses.

The grey pieces at the back right in steps 4-5 may be the orange plates (b4, b5) and the bracket (b6) from page 2. The pictures appear to show them differently. I did not add or remove anything for them.
The tile b12 is assumed to sit on the stud of b11. The red plate b14 is assumed to sit on a stud of the grate b13.
Page 4 starts a new small sub-model, the yellow piece shown in the inset. It is separate from the main model so far, with a new first piece b15.

Step 1: dark grey 2x2 plate (b15). Step 2: two side-handle plates (b16, b17) attached under it. Step 3: yellow 3x2 rounded plate (b18). Step 4: yellow slope (b19) at the left end of b18, then a second yellow 3x2 rounded plate (b20) is added with the red arrows.
I assumed b20 rests only on b18, offset toward the right so it does not cover the slope. The sizes in the pictures are small, so this is a best guess.

Page 5, step 8: the small yellow sub-assembly from page 4 (b15-b20) is pushed onto the main body from the left, as the arrow shows. The picture is small. I took the join to be the stud of a dark grey round brick (b8) going through the hole in b20. Which of b8 or b9 it is is a guess.

Step 9: two dark grey round plates are added on the studs at the left of the sub-assembly (b21, b22). I took them to be the 6141 parts, but they could be a different grey part, and which studs of b20 they go on is a guess.

Page 6 shows steps 10-11. Step 10: a black 2x4 plate (b23) goes on top of the main body, and a yellow clip plate (b24) with a trans-yellow tile (b25) goes on the left sub-assembly. Step 11: two trans-brown 1x2 bricks (b26, b27) go side by side on b23, and a yellow door-rail plate (b28) goes on the left.
The pictures are small, so the positions and the supports (rests_on) of these pieces are best guesses.
The black plate b23 is assumed to rest on b7, b8 and b9. The tile b25 is assumed to sit on the stud of b24. The door-rail plate b28 is assumed to cover the two dark grey round plates b21 and b22.

Page 7, step 12 of the main model: a yellow 2x3 plate (b29) goes on top of the two trans-brown bricks, and a black bar piece (b30) is clipped on at the front left. The picture seems to show two arms at the left, but I only recorded one bar. I assumed it clips to b24.

Page 7 right side starts a new small sub-assembly (steps 1-2): two dark grey side-handle plates (b31, b32) are pushed together. The parts list shows no unplaced lego-2540 at this point, so the 2540 count (4 in the list) is exceeded. I used lego-2540 anyway because the pieces look like it. Earlier assumptions about the 2540s under b1 and b15 may be wrong.
How the two plates in the sub-assembly join is a guess from the small pictures.

Page 8, step 3: two dark grey 2x2 plates (b33, b34) go side by side across the 1x4 handle block (b31, b32) to make the 2x4 top. Step 4: a black 1x2x1 panel (b35) goes at the left end of the top as the bucket wall.

Step 4 seems to show a wall at the end and along the back of the bucket, but only one panel fits the parts I can see, so this step is a guess. Other pieces (such as the 1x4 plate or the corner panels) may be added on later pages.
Step 13: the finished bucket is pushed onto the arm (arrow), clipped to the bar b30 at the front left. I took the handle of b31 as the part that clips.

Page 9 has one step (14) and shows the digger with its four wheels fitted. The booklet shows no separate wheel-building steps, so I assumed this step adds both 4600 wheel-holder plates, four wheels and four tyres.
I assumed the wheel-holder plates fit under the base plate b1. This may clash with the side-handle plates b2 and b3 that I put under b1 on page 2, so it is a best guess.

The picture also shows a brown round piece on the roof, but I added no new piece for it, because the parts list shows no trans-orange pieces left to place at this point. I assumed it is one of the earlier trans-orange plates (b4 or b5).
This seems to be the finished main model. The parts still unplaced are probably for the alternative models later in the booklet.
Page 10 starts the second model, the quad bike shown in the inset. It is built from the same set of bricks, so the parts used here come from the unplaced list.

Step 1: the black grate slope (b47) goes on the right end of the dark grey 1x4 plate (b46). Step 2: it is joined to a yellow plate (b48). I used the 3x2 rounded plate as the only yellow plate left that fits, and the placement is a guess.

Step 3 shows the assembly turned over, with a dark grey handle/bar piece under the left end and a thin yellow strip underneath. I could not identify the handle piece clearly, so I did not record it. It may be the bar-up plate lego-88072, to be checked on the next page.
Page 11, step 4: the chassis is turned over and a light grey wheel-holder plate (b49, b50) is fitted at each end of the underside. The side pegs at the ends are the holders' wheel pegs.
These two 4600 plates come from the first model, which was taken apart, so they duplicate b36 and b37. The unplaced list does not include them. I gave them new ids because this is a new model.
Step 5: the chassis is turned back over and nothing new is added.
Which plate the holders attach to (b48 or b46) is a guess from the small pictures.

Page 12, step 6: a yellow slope (b51) is added at the front left of the quad bike chassis. It looks different from step 5, but the picture is small, so this is a guess. I assumed it sits on the yellow plate b48.

Right side starts a new small sub-assembly shown in the inset (steps 1-2). Step 1: a yellow 1x2 door-rail plate (b52). Step 2: a yellow clip plate (b53, b54) is added at each end. These are probably the handlebars and they will be attached to the bike on a later page.
The pictures are small, so how the clip plates join the door-rail plate is a guess.
Page 13 continues the handlebar sub-assembly of the quad bike (b52-b54). Step 3 appears to show the same assembly from the side, so I added nothing for it.
Step 4 (2x): a trans-yellow tile is put on a yellow clip plate, built twice (b55 + b56 and b57 + b58). I assumed each unit is attached sideways to the door-rail plate b52.
The 4081b and 3070b pieces here are duplicates, since the unplaced list had none left. They come from the first model, which was taken apart.

Steps 5-6: I guessed a dark grey bar-up plate (b59) and the black bar piece (b60) clipped to it. The pictures show dark grey plates with handles that I could not identify, and a stick with a round end. I did not record the round end, or the 6141, 6231 and 4274 pieces that are still unplaced. This part is low confidence.
Page 14, step 7: a pin (b61) is added at the right end of the black bar piece (b60) on the handlebar sub-assembly. The picture is small, so which piece it goes into is a guess.

Step 8: the handlebar sub-assembly is pushed onto the chassis from the left, as the arrow shows. I assumed it joins the yellow chassis plate b48 through the dark grey plate b59. Nothing else new is added.
Still unplaced after this page: two dark grey round plates and two black corner panels.
Page 15, step 9: a dark grey round plate (b62) goes onto a stud of the dark grey plate b46, as the arrow shows.

Step 10: two trans-brown 1x2 bricks (b63, b64) form a 2x2 block on the plate, and a second dark grey round plate (b65) goes on top of the block. The bricks are duplicates of b26 and b27, because the unplaced list has none left. They come from the first model.
The pictures are small, so which studs these pieces use is a guess. I assumed the block sits on b46, with b62 on a different stud, and that b65 sits on the block.
The two black corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

Page 16, step 11: three trans-orange round plates are stacked on a stud of the seat block (b66, b67, b68). The orange plates are duplicates, since the unplaced list has none left. They come from the first model.

Step 12: a yellow slope (b69) goes at the front of the seat block. Four wheels and four tyres (b70-b77) are fitted to the wheel holders b49 and b50. These are also duplicates of earlier pieces. Which side each wheel goes on is a guess.
The yellow slope was not shown in step 11, so I assumed it is new in step 12 and sits on b64. The two black corner panels (6231) are still unplaced. They may be used in the remaining pages.

Page 17 starts the third model, shown in the inset (a buggy). It is built from the same bricks, so these pieces are duplicates of earlier ones, taken from the taken-apart models. The unplaced list only has the two black corner panels left.

Step 1: a yellow 2x3 plate (b79) goes on a black 2x4 plate (b78). Step 2: a second black 2x4 plate (b80) is added to the left, with the yellow plate bridging the two. Step 3: a yellow mudguard (b81) is added on top of the left side.
The pictures are small, so how the second black plate overlaps the first and where the mudguard sits are guesses.
Step 3 also shows ridged pegs at the left end, probably wheel holders. I did not record them, because I could not tell clearly which part they are. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.
Page 18, step 4: a yellow 3x2 rounded plate (b82) goes on the right end of the buggy chassis. The yellow wedge at the left is the mudguard b81 from page 17, so I added nothing new for it.
Step 5: the chassis is turned over and a light grey wheel-holder plate (b83, b84) is fitted at each end. These duplicate earlier 4600 pieces, taken from the taken-apart models.
Which black plate each holder attaches to is a guess from the small pictures. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

Page 19 shows steps 6-7 of the buggy. Step 6: the chassis is turned back over, a black 1x2x1 panel (b85) goes in the middle as a wall, and a yellow door-rail plate (b86) goes on the studs of the yellow rounded plate. Step 7: a black grate slope (b87) goes on the left, and two trans-orange round plates are stacked on the right (b88, b89).
These are duplicates of pieces from the earlier models, since the unplaced list only has the corner panels left.
The supports (rests_on) are guesses from the small pictures. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

Page 20, step 8: two black corner panels (b90, b91) go beside the wall panel, and a yellow bracket (b92) goes at the rear right end. Step 9: two trans-brown 1x2 bricks (b93, b94) form a 2x2 block next to the panels.

The pictures are small, so I could not identify the exact studs. I assumed the corner panels sit on the black plate b78 and the bracket sits on the door-rail plate b86. The bricks duplicate earlier ones, from the taken-apart models.
The trans-orange plates stacked on b86 in step 7 are no longer visible in step 8. I assumed the bracket now covers them. If they were removed instead, b88 and b89 should be dropped.

Page 21, step 10: a second pair of trans-brown 1x2 bricks (b95, b96) is added beside the first (b93, b94). Two trans-red round plates (b97, b98) are pushed on the sides of the yellow bracket b92. Only one arrow is drawn, but the picture shows a red piece on each side.

Step 11: a black bar piece (b99) is added as an arc at the back. I took it to clip around the red plate b97. The picture is small, so this is a guess. I did not record any dark grey end pieces on the bar.
All pieces in the parts list are now placed, so this page again uses duplicates from the taken-apart models. Positions and supports are guesses.

Page 22, step 12: a yellow 2x3 plate (b100) goes on top of the four trans-brown bricks, with two yellow clip plates carrying trans-yellow tiles (b101 + b102, b103 + b104). The picture shows one clearly at the back left, and I assumed a second one next to it. This is a guess.
Step 13: four wheels with tyres (b105-b112) are fitted to the wheel holders b83 and b84. Which side each wheel goes on is a guess.
All pieces here are duplicates of pieces from the taken-apart models, since the parts list is already used up.
Back cover with adverts for other LEGO Creator sets. There is no building step, so nothing is added.

[L3] Not a real problem. The booklet is a 3-in-1 set and builds three separate models one after another: the digger (pages 2-9), the quad bike (pages 10-16) and the buggy (pages 17-22). The three groups are meant to be unconnected. Inside each model I joined the sub-assemblies to the main body.

[L4] Not a real problem for the 'pieces not in the list' part. The set has only 57 pieces. Each later model is built from the bricks of the one before, after it is taken apart. A piece is therefore listed once per model it is used in, with a new id each time, because ids are never reused. That is why the counts go over the parts list for types such as 3020, 6141, 3065, 4081b, 3070b, 3021 and 4600. The three models are separate, so the physical pieces are never in two places at once.

Two counts are different. Within the digger alone, lego-2540 is used six times (b2, b3, b16, b17, b31, b32) but the list has four. I could not read the small pictures well enough to say which of these handle plates are really something else. Please check them against a larger scan.
I have not removed any earlier pieces, as the instruction says additions only, so nothing is added here.

Three unconnected groups is correct. Inside each model the sub-assemblies are joined to the main body, so I added no links between the models.

So a brick appears once per model that uses it, with a new id each time because ids are never reused. This is why counts for 3020, 6141, 3065, 4081b, 3070b, 3021, 4600 and others go over the parts list. The three models are never built at the same time.

One count may be a real error. Within the digger alone, lego-2540 appears six times (b2, b3, b16, b17, b31, b32) but the list has four. The pictures were too small for me to tell which of them are really other handle or bar parts. I did not remove any earlier pieces, as only additions are allowed, so please check these against a larger scan.
Nothing is added in this reply.

Page 13 continues the handlebar sub-assembly of the quad bike (b52-b54). Step 3 appears to show the same assembly from the side, so I added nothing for it.
Step 4 (2x): a trans-yellow tile is put on a yellow clip plate, built twice (b55 + b56 and b57 + b58). I assumed each unit is attached sideways to the door-rail plate b52.

The pictures show dark grey plates with handles that I could not identify, and a stick with a round end. I did not record the round end, or the 6141, 6231 and 4274 pieces that are still unplaced. This part is low confidence.
Page 14, step 7: a pin (b61) is added at the right end of the black bar piece (b60) on the handlebar sub-assembly. The picture is small, so which piece it goes into is a guess.

Step 8: the handlebar sub-assembly is pushed onto the chassis from the left, as the arrow shows. I assumed it joins the yellow chassis plate b48 through the dark grey plate b59. Nothing else new is added.
Still unplaced after this page: two dark grey round plates and two black corner panels.
Page 15, step 9: a dark grey round plate (b62) goes onto a stud of the dark grey plate b46, as the arrow shows.

Step 10: two trans-brown 1x2 bricks (b63, b64) form a 2x2 block on the plate, and a second dark grey round plate (b65) goes on top of the block. The bricks are duplicates of b26 and b27, because the unplaced list has none left. They come from the first model.
The pictures are small, so which studs these pieces use is a guess. I assumed the block sits on b46, with b62 on a different stud, and that b65 sits on the block.
The two black corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

Page 16, step 11: three trans-orange round plates are stacked on a stud of the seat block (b66, b67, b68). The orange plates are duplicates, since the unplaced list has none left. They come from the first model.

Step 12: a yellow slope (b69) goes at the front of the seat block. Four wheels and four tyres (b70-b77) are fitted to the wheel holders b49 and b50. These are also duplicates of earlier pieces. Which side each wheel goes on is a guess.
The yellow slope was not shown in step 11, so I assumed it is new in step 12 and sits on b64. The two black corner panels (6231) are still unplaced. They may be used in the remaining pages.

Page 17 starts the third model, shown in the inset (a buggy). It is built from the same bricks, so these pieces are duplicates of earlier ones, taken from the taken-apart models. The unplaced list only has the two black corner panels left.

Step 1: a yellow 2x3 plate (b79) goes on a black 2x4 plate (b78). Step 2: a second black 2x4 plate (b80) is added to the left, with the yellow plate bridging the two. Step 3: a yellow mudguard (b81) is added on top of the left side.
The pictures are small, so how the second black plate overlaps the first and where the mudguard sits are guesses.
Step 3 also shows ridged pegs at the left end, probably wheel holders. I did not record them, because I could not tell clearly which part they are. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.
Page 18, step 4: a yellow 3x2 rounded plate (b82) goes on the right end of the buggy chassis. The yellow wedge at the left is the mudguard b81 from page 17, so I added nothing new for it.
Step 5: the chassis is turned over and a light grey wheel-holder plate (b83, b84) is fitted at each end. These duplicate earlier 4600 pieces, taken from the taken-apart models.
Which black plate each holder attaches to is a guess from the small pictures. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

Page 19 shows steps 6-7 of the buggy. Step 6: the chassis is turned back over, a black 1x2x1 panel (b85) goes in the middle as a wall, and a yellow door-rail plate (b86) goes on the studs of the yellow rounded plate. Step 7: a black grate slope (b87) goes on the left, and two trans-orange round plates are stacked on the right (b88, b89).
These are duplicates of pieces from the earlier models, since the unplaced list only has the corner panels left.
The supports (rests_on) are guesses from the small pictures. The corner panels (6231) are still unplaced.

The trans-orange plates stacked on b86 in step 7 are no longer visible in step 8. I assumed the bracket now covers them. If they were removed instead, b88 and b89 should be dropped.

Step 11: a black bar piece (b99) is added as an arc at the back. I took it to clip around the red plate b97. The picture is small, so this is a guess. I did not record any dark grey end pieces on the bar.
All pieces in the parts list are now placed, so this page again uses duplicates from the taken-apart models. Positions and supports are guesses.

Page 22, step 12: a yellow 2x3 plate (b100) goes on top of the four trans-brown bricks, with two yellow clip plates carrying trans-yellow tiles (b101 + b102, b103 + b104). The picture shows one clearly at the back left, and I assumed a second one next to it. This is a guess.
